Nxeon (VPS/game-hosting business, production Next.js app at /opt/nxeon). Two real admin-panel table upgrades requested by the owner from live screenshots tonight.

IMPORTANT PROCESS RULE (a real production outage happened earlier tonight from multiple agents each running their own build/deploy concurrently): **do NOT run `deploy-staging.sh` or `promote-production.sh` yourself.** Before starting, run `ps aux | grep -E "next build|deploy-staging|promote-production"` — if anything is running, wait. Commit and push to `main`, then STOP without deploying. Other agents are concurrently working on unrelated Nxeon features in this same shared tree — check `git status`/`git log` before/after, and if you see uncommitted changes that aren't yours, never `git add -A`, stage only your own files by exact path.

## 1. Clients table: real acquisition source

Find the admin Clients page (`645 accounts`, columns: Client / Role / Servers / Balance / Monthly spend / Joined / Actions — likely `app/admin/**/clients/page.tsx` or similar). The owner wants to see where each customer came from: (a) any real "how did you hear about us" survey/signup-form answer if one is captured anywhere in this app (check the `User` model and signup flow for an existing field — search for "how did you hear", "hearAbout", "referralSource", "signupSource" or similar before assuming it doesn't exist), and (b) real marketing attribution if it's been captured — check for existing UTM/referrer/ad-click tracking (this session's memory mentions a real Meta Pixel/CAPI integration and Google Ads offline-conversion upload exist in this codebase — search for how/where that attribution data is stored, e.g. a `first_touch_source`, `utm_source`, `fbclid`/`gclid`-derived field, likely on `User` or a related signup-analytics table). Add a real column (or an expandable/tooltip detail, your call on the best UI given how much real data actually exists per user) showing whatever REAL source data exists — if most users have no captured source (a real, honest possibility), say so in your report rather than padding the UI with fake fallback text like "Direct" for someone with genuinely no data; use an honest "Unknown" or similar instead. Do not fabricate attribution data.

## 2. Server Fleet table: more room, real search/filter, more columns

Find the admin Server Fleet page (`33 servers across all clients`, columns: Hostname / Owner / Plan / VMID / SSH Endpoint / Node / Region / Resources / Status — likely `app/admin/**/servers/page.tsx` or similar).
- **Wider margins**: the table currently feels cramped against the page edges — widen the container to give more room (check what other admin pages/tables in this app use for their content width and match that convention rather than inventing a new one).
- **Real search/filter**: add a search input that filters by hostname, owner (customer name/email), plan/service name, AND node — combinable, real (server-side query or real client-side filter over already-loaded rows, your call based on how many total server rows typically load here — check the real total count first via a DB query before deciding server-side vs client-side is more appropriate).
- **More columns per row**: add (a) a real "Reboot" action button per row (check `lib/actions-admin-servers.ts` or wherever admin server actions live for an existing reboot/restart action to call — reuse it, don't invent a new mechanism; if only a customer-facing restart action exists and no admin-specific one does, that's worth flagging in your report rather than building unsafe admin-impersonation logic yourself), (b) a real "Provision date" column (check the `Server` model for a real creation/provisioned timestamp field — likely `createdAt` or a dedicated `provisionedAt`), (c) a real "Total spent" column reflecting lifetime revenue from this server INCLUDING add-ons (check how billing/invoices are modeled — likely a real `Invoice`/`Order`/`Payment` table keyed to the server or its owning subscription — sum the real historical charges, don't estimate from the current plan price × months elapsed, since that would miss real add-ons/price changes/discounts).

## Process (mandatory)
- Read the actual current page/component files, the `User`/`Server` Prisma models, and any existing attribution/billing-history code in full before editing — find real file paths via `grep`/`find`, don't guess.
- DB reads only via `db` from `lib/db`, exploratory scripts under `scripts/_tmp-*.ts` via `npx tsx`, deleted after. NEVER print/construct a raw psql/DATABASE_URL string.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Commit and push to `main` (one commit per feature is fine).
- Add a dated entry to `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`.

Report back: exactly what real acquisition-source data exists today (and how much of the customer base actually has it populated vs. unknown), the real reboot-action mechanism you reused (or the gap you found if none exists), and confirmation the "total spent" figure is a real historical sum, not an estimate.

  never copies one onto the `User` row. But every authenticated pageview also stamps `Visit.userId`
  under the SAME `visitorId` cookie the person had before signing up, so a real (not fabricated) join
  is possible: find the visitorId(s) a user's authenticated visits used, then find the earliest visit
  under any of those visitorIds that carries a utm/gclid tag. Checked live: this recovers a real
  first-touch source for 253 of the 645 accounts.

New "Source" column shows the self-reported answer when given (brand badge), else the derived
tracked first-touch (slate badge, hover for the exact tag + date), else "Skipped survey", else a
